title: The Glasshouse Oath
summary: SirLocked and his companion investigate the death of Professor Elian Marrow at Bellweather Glasshouse, where a priceless night-blooming orchid vanished during a midnight lamp failure. Across the glasshouse, pump room, study, and old orchid cellar, the investigators must compare botanical traces, fractured alibis, and the household's guarded oath to discover who carefully pruned the truth.

characters.name: Livia Marrow
characters.description: Poised, observant, and wounded by years of withheld approval. Livia inherits Bellweather but seems more frightened by the family oath than pleased by the estate.

characters.name: Dr. Cassian Voss
characters.description: A polished academic whose admiration for Marrow conceals a bruising professional rivalry over orchid classification and public recognition.

characters.name: Marta Quill
characters.description: Practical, blunt, and fiercely loyal to the living collection. Marta knows every valve and walkway in the glasshouse, and she resents anyone who treats plants as trophies.

characters.name: Silas Fen
characters.description: Charming, evasive, and financially pressed. Silas has foreign buyers, bad debts, and an obvious interest in the missing orchid.

characters.name: Reverend Halden Pike
characters.description: Soft-spoken and insistent on peace. Reverend Pike has long mediated Bellweather family matters and invokes the old Glasshouse Oath whenever questions become dangerous.

clues.title: Glass Fallen the Wrong Way
clues.content: The largest display shards lie outward from the orchid pedestal rather than inward from the roofline, suggesting the shattered panes were disturbed after the orchid was already handled.
clues.visualDescription: A crescent of long glass shards fans away from the empty pedestal across the tiled walkway, with smaller safety fragments still clinging to the upper frame.
clues.inventoryDescription: Photograph of glass shards fanning outward from the orchid display.
clues.narrativeMeaning: The scene was staged to look like a chaotic accident, but the break pattern does not match a simple fall from above.

clues.title: Gray Mineral Footprint by the Service Door
clues.content: A pale gray footprint at the glasshouse service door contains mineral grit unlike the black greenhouse soil. It matches powder used around the pump room charity hampers and chapel stores.
clues.visualDescription: A partial boot print in damp condensation beside the service door, its sole packed with light gray grit rather than dark potting soil.
clues.inventoryDescription: Photograph of a gray mineral footprint at the service door.
clues.narrativeMeaning: Someone entered or left through the service way after passing through an area connected to the mineral springs or chapel stores.

clues.title: Dry Ring on the Orchid Pedestal
clues.content: The pedestal is wet with lamp-mist except for a dry circular ring where the orchid pot sat. The ring has sharply dried edges, meaning the pot was removed several minutes before the lamps failed.
clues.visualDescription: An empty marble pedestal with beads of moisture everywhere except a clean dry circle at the center, its edge visibly crisp under returning lamplight.
clues.inventoryDescription: Photograph of the dry pot ring on the wet orchid pedestal.
clues.narrativeMeaning: The orchid theft was not a spontaneous act during the darkness; it began before the public blackout.

clues.title: Green Tying Twine on the Vent Latch
clues.content: A strand of green gardener's twine is caught on the vent latch, seeming to implicate Marta. The strand is brittle and sun-faded, likely from an old plant tie rather than tonight's work.
clues.visualDescription: A faded green fiber snagged on a brass vent latch above the broken display area, dry and frayed at both ends.
clues.inventoryDescription: Photograph of old green twine snagged on the vent latch.
clues.narrativeMeaning: It points suspiciously toward the gardener at first, but its age makes it a misleading trace rather than proof.

clues.title: Silas Fen's Debt Telegram
clues.content: A telegram tucked beside a pump room saucer demands payment from Silas by dawn and mentions a foreign buyer seeking 'night stock of exceptional rarity.'
clues.visualDescription: A folded telegram under a mineral-water saucer, with the words 'payment by dawn' and 'foreign buyer' visible through damp paper.
clues.inventoryDescription: Photograph of Silas Fen's urgent debt telegram.
clues.narrativeMeaning: Silas had a powerful motive to steal the orchid, but the document alone does not place him inside the glasshouse at the decisive time.

clues.title: Voss Saw a Gray-Dusted Figure
clues.content: Pressed on his pump room alibi, Dr. Voss admits he saw a gray-dusted figure pass from the corridor toward Bellweather just after midnight, but he kept silent to avoid being drawn into scandal.
clues.visualDescription: No physical photograph; this clue is recorded as SirLocked's interview note after confronting Voss.
clues.inventoryDescription: Interview note: Voss saw a gray-dusted figure heading toward the estate.
clues.narrativeMeaning: The footprint trace corresponds to a witnessed movement, tightening the timeline around the service route.

clues.title: Chapel Charity Hampers with Mineral Powder
clues.content: The pump room charity hampers are dusted with pale mineral powder from spring-salt wrappings. Their labels show Reverend Pike was arranging delivery through the chapel vestry shortly before midnight.
clues.visualDescription: Stacked wicker hampers marked for the chapel vestry, their handles and nearby floor dusted with the same pale gray powder seen in the glasshouse print.
clues.inventoryDescription: Photograph of mineral-dusted chapel charity hampers.
clues.narrativeMeaning: The gray powder is tied to Pike's movements, not to ordinary garden work.

clues.title: Blotter Impression Naming Pike
clues.content: The professor's desk blotter preserves a reversed impression: 'Pike trustee sales... Oath clause void if concealed.' Marrow had evidence connecting Pike to improper sales from the Bellweather collection.
clues.visualDescription: A green leather blotter under angled light, showing faint reversed words pressed into the surface beside an empty rectangle where a journal had lain.
clues.inventoryDescription: Photograph of the blotter impression naming Pike and the oath clause.
clues.narrativeMeaning: This supplies a concealed motive: the professor was preparing to expose Pike's abuse of his trustee position.

clues.title: Livia's Lawyer Appointment
clues.content: A calendar entry and rain-spotted calling card show Livia had already arranged to meet a solicitor about refusing immediate sale of Bellweather, undermining the idea that she urgently killed for inheritance.
clues.visualDescription: A desk calendar opened to the following morning with 'Harrow & Vale, estate restraint' written beside a solicitor's damp calling card.
clues.narrativeMeaning: Livia had inheritance concerns, but her documented plan points to preserving the estate rather than profiting from murder.

clues.title: Livia Reveals the Oath's Silence
clues.content: After being confronted with the blotter, Livia admits the household swore not to discuss the old Glasshouse Oath: a trustee scandal could strip Bellweather's private collection and expose years of quiet sales.
clues.visualDescription: No physical photograph; this clue is recorded as an interview note after confronting Livia with the blotter.
clues.inventoryDescription: Interview note: Livia explains why the oath frightened the household.
clues.narrativeMeaning: The oath was not sentimental family folklore; it was a legal and social threat to whoever had exploited the collection.

clues.title: Chapel Wax and Cassock Fiber on the Service Hatch
clues.content: The cellar-side service hatch bears fresh chapel taper wax and a black wool fiber consistent with Reverend Pike's cassock. The hatch gives direct access to the glasshouse service door and lamp control line.
clues.visualDescription: A low iron hatch with a smear of amber candle wax on the latch plate and a short black wool fiber caught in a splinter near the pull chain.
clues.inventoryDescription: Photograph of chapel wax and black fiber on the cellar service hatch.
clues.narrativeMeaning: This is the strongest late physical link between Pike and the hidden route used to stage the blackout and move the orchid.

clues.title: Hidden Crate with Orchid and Journal
clues.content: Behind old propagation frames is a ventilated crate containing the missing orchid and Marrow's research journal. The crate is sealed with a chapel-office paper band bearing Pike's impression.
clues.visualDescription: A slatted crate tucked behind dusty frames, with pale orchid petals visible through the vents and a broken paper band stamped with the chapel office seal.
clues.inventoryDescription: Photograph of the hidden orchid crate and missing journal.
clues.narrativeMeaning: The stolen object and the motive document were hidden together by someone with chapel materials and access.

dialogues.question: What did your uncle intend to announce at the midnight viewing?
dialogues.answer: Only the orchid's bloom, I thought. Uncle enjoyed ceremony. If there was another announcement, he kept it from me, as he kept most approvals.

dialogues.question: Several people mention a Glasshouse Oath. What is it?
dialogues.answer: An old family phrase. A promise to protect the collection and not disgrace Bellweather. Reverend Pike says repeating it now will only wound the living.

dialogues.question: Who could operate the glasshouse vents and lamps?
dialogues.answer: Any fool can pull a chain if shown where it hangs. Knowing which chain matters is another thing. I checked the vents at half-eleven; they were sound then.

dialogues.question: Why are you so certain this was an accident?
dialogues.answer: Because grief seeks villains when it cannot bear chance. Professor Marrow was old, the glass was treacherous, and no good comes from dragging sacred family vows into public mud.

dialogues.question: Where were you when the lamps failed?
dialogues.answer: In the pump room by the north windows, alone with a glass of the most sulfurous water in England. I saw no one of consequence pass toward Bellweather.

dialogues.question: Your debts make the vanished orchid convenient. Did you arrange a buyer?
dialogues.answer: A dealer hears offers. Hearing is not stealing, and stealing is not murder. I meant to bid on cuttings when Marrow's vanity cooled.

dialogues.question: Why are the chapel charity hampers dusted with the same gray mineral powder found at the glasshouse?
dialogues.answer: The hampers were packed from the spring stores. I carried some, yes, but only before the viewing. Charity leaves dust on honest sleeves.

dialogues.question: Could the orchid be sold quickly?
dialogues.answer: Not whole. Too famous. A smuggler would divide it, ruin it, and still attract every customs man from here to Calais. The journal may be worth more than the plant to the right enemy.

dialogues.question: Did inheriting Bellweather solve your difficulties?
dialogues.answer: It multiplies them. I asked a solicitor how to keep the estate intact, not how to sell it. Uncle never believed I would choose duty without being forced.

dialogues.question: Was your feud with Professor Marrow serious enough to steal his journal?
dialogues.answer: His classifications were infuriating and often correct. I wanted to defeat him in print, not rummage through his drawers like a housebreaker.

dialogues.question: The blotter names Reverend Pike and trustee sales. Did your uncle discuss this?
dialogues.answer: No. That is, not plainly. He told me some promises rot if kept in darkness, but he never said Pike's name to me.

dialogues.question: Who knew the old cellar hatch still opened into the glasshouse service way?
dialogues.answer: I knew, Marrow knew, and Reverend Pike knew from blessing the old orchid house after the fever year. Silas could guess; Voss would never soil his cuffs unless fame required it.

dialogues.question: The orchid and journal were hidden in the cellar. Is this your crate?
dialogues.answer: No dealer hides a prize under its owner's house with a chapel seal on it. If I had stolen that plant, it would already be three counties away and nameless.

dialogues.question: How do you explain chapel wax, cassock fiber, and the hidden crate below the orchid house?
dialogues.answer: Bellweather is full of old chapel things. Wax travels on hands; fibers travel on air. As for the crate, I beg you to consider what scandal will do to Livia and to every servant here.

evidenceChallenges.prompt: Which evidence contradicts Voss's claim that he saw no one of consequence pass toward Bellweather?
evidenceChallenges.successResponse: Voss stiffens and concedes the gray trace matters. He admits seeing a gray-dusted figure move from the pump corridor toward the estate shortly after midnight.
evidenceChallenges.failureResponse: Voss dismisses the point as gossip dressed as deduction. A stronger physical trace is needed to make him amend his account.

evidenceChallenges.prompt: Which evidence proves Livia knows more about the oath and Pike's trustee trouble than she first admitted?
evidenceChallenges.successResponse: Livia's composure breaks. She admits the oath was being used to silence talk of trustee sales and that her uncle meant to expose the truth.
evidenceChallenges.failureResponse: Livia retreats into family propriety. Her denial needs to be tested against the professor's own surviving trace.

deductions.prompt: Which chain best explains the death, the vanished orchid, and the household's oath?

options.label: Pike removed the orchid before the blackout, used the cellar hatch and lamp line to stage an accident, and hid both orchid and journal to suppress Marrow's proof of trustee sales.
Silas stole the orchid for a buyer during the darkness, and the professor died accidentally when pursuing him through unstable display glass.
Marta triggered the lamps and vents to protect the collection from sale, then planted chapel traces to punish Reverend Pike.

deductions.successResponse: The clues align: the orchid was gone before the darkness, the service route bears Pike's chapel traces, and the journal explains why the oath had become dangerous.
deductions.failureResponse: That chain leaves either the early removal, the chapel-marked hatch, or the trustee motive unexplained.

requiredTeamworkChains.description: One investigator documents the cellar hatch's chapel wax and cassock fiber while the other presses Livia on the blotter impression, linking physical access to the suppressed oath motive before forming the final accusation.

hints.text: Photograph what the blackout should not have changed: the direction of broken glass, the moisture on the pedestal, and traces near the service door.
The pump room is full of public gossip, but the useful evidence is practical: who handled mineral powder and who pretends not to have seen movement.
Marrow's missing journal left impressions behind. Look for traces on the writing surface and documents that complicate obvious inheritance motives.
The cellar should be dusty and unused. Fresh marks, chapel materials, and hidden storage are more important than old gardening clutter.
Voss claims no one passed toward Bellweather. Use evidence that proves someone did use the service approach.
Livia minimizes the oath. Confront her with the professor's own trace connecting the oath to a named trustee.
Build the chain in three parts: the orchid was moved before the blackout, the cellar route shows who could stage it, and the study reveals why the journal had to vanish.

finalLogic.motive: Reverend Pike had secretly profited from improper trustee sales of Bellweather specimens. Professor Marrow's missing journal and planned announcement would expose the fraud and void the protective silence of the Glasshouse Oath.
finalLogic.method: Pike removed the orchid before the lamps failed, used the old cellar service hatch to reach the glasshouse lamp control line, staged the shattering glass as an accident during the darkness, and hid the orchid with Marrow's journal in a chapel-sealed crate below the old orchid house.

motiveOptions.label: To prevent Marrow from exposing Pike's trustee sales and the legal danger hidden inside the Glasshouse Oath.
To help Livia inherit Bellweather before Marrow could disinherit her.
To sell the orchid to a foreign buyer and pay private gambling debts.

methodOptions.label: Remove the orchid before the blackout, enter by the cellar hatch, interrupt the lamps, stage the glass break, and hide the orchid with the journal.
Break the roof panes from outside during the storm, causing an accidental fall while stealing the orchid afterward.
Poison the professor with orchid pollen, then scatter glass to conceal the true cause.

finalLogic.winEnding: SirLocked lays the photographs in order: the early-dry pedestal ring, the gray service-door print, the blotter naming Pike, and the chapel-marked cellar hatch. Pike's appeal to silence collapses when the hidden crate reveals both orchid and journal. The professor's death is no longer a sad accident but a staged crime born of trustee fraud and fear. Livia releases the Glasshouse Oath to lawful scrutiny, Marta returns the orchid to controlled care, and Veyrbridge learns that some vows protect truth only when they are finally spoken aloud.
finalLogic.failEnding: The accusation falters around gossip and obvious motives. Silas's debts and Marta's access muddy the account, allowing Pike to urge discretion until the inquiry cools. The orchid survives in hiding for a time, but Marrow's journal disappears again, and the Glasshouse Oath remains a polished phrase covering an unpruned lie.
